subject.title: Gateway runtime: "no such table: plugin_state_entries / acp_sessions" despite tables existing in state/openclaw.sqlite (agent turns produce no reply)

question: Should maintainers require runtime database-path proof before a fix PR, or treat the reporter's paired table errors as enough to start a Docker regression/fix now?
rationale: Source inspection shows the intended shared DB path, but the reported contradiction depends on live process path resolution; choosing a fix without that proof could patch the wrong boundary.

options.title: Collect Path Proof First
options.body: Ask for redacted OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR, resolved openOpenClawStateDatabase path, and PRAGMA database_list output from the failing gateway process before selecting the fix boundary.

options.title: Build Current-Main Repro
options.body: Use the report to create a Docker regression that exercises gateway run, device-pair notify polling, chat.history, and sessions.send with DB path diagnostics enabled.

options.title: Fold Into Startup Migration Follow-Up
options.body: Only choose this if maintainers believe the merged container-upgrade checkpoint is the right owner and this issue should become a verification/follow-up against that path.

recommendation.title: Collect Path Proof First
recommendation.body: Ask for redacted OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR, resolved openOpenClawStateDatabase path, and PRAGMA database_list output from the failing gateway process before selecting the fix boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete owns the strongest history signal for shared SQLite state and ACP metadata persistence, which is the decision boundary here.
